title: Highest-Protein Vegetables: Which Ones Actually Provide the Most?

seo.title: Highest-Protein Vegetables: A Practical Ranking
seo.meta_description: Compare Brussels sprouts, artichokes, kale, spinach, broccoli and asparagus by protein, and see why vegetables still aren't concentrated protein foods.
seo.search_intent: Rank vegetables by protein while correcting misleading per-calorie claims.

excerpt: Vegetables contribute protein, but their high water content keeps the absolute amount modest. Brussels sprouts, artichokes, kale, spinach and broccoli generally provide about 3 grams per 100 grams.
content_html:
Broccoli is sometimes advertised as “surprisingly high in protein.” The surprise comes from looking at protein as a percentage of very few calories. In absolute terms, most vegetables contain only 2–4 grams per 100 grams because they are mostly water.

Representative ranking

VegetableApprox. protein/100 g
Brussels sprouts3–4 g
Artichoke3–3.5 g
Kaleabout 3 g
Spinach2.9 g
Broccoli2.8 g
Asparagus2.2 g
Cauliflower1.9 g

What about peas?

Green peas provide roughly 5–6 g per 100 g and are sold as a vegetable, but botanically they are legumes. We exclude them from the main table to keep the categories consistent.

Broccoli in context

A generous 200 g serving may contribute 5–6 g of protein. That is meaningful as part of a meal, but far below a serving of beans, tofu, eggs, fish or chicken.

Leafy greens shrink when cooked

Spinach and kale lose volume during cooking, making it easy to eat more grams. Protein per 100 g can also change with water loss. They remain more important for micronutrients, fiber and phytochemicals than as stand-alone protein foods.

The protein-per-calorie trick

Because broccoli is so low in calories, a substantial fraction of those calories come from protein. But reaching 30 grams of protein would require roughly a kilogram. Percentages do not replace serving size.

Use vegetables to add, not replace

Pair broccoli with tofu, spinach with lentils, Brussels sprouts with salmon, or a vegetable soup with beans. The protein adds up while vegetables perform their main role: providing fiber, volume and micronutrients.

Frequently asked questions

Which vegetable has the most protein?

Among common non-legume vegetables, Brussels sprouts and artichokes are near the top at roughly 3–4 g per 100 g.

Does broccoli have more protein than beef per calorie?

Percentage-based comparisons can produce that impression, but beef is vastly more concentrated in protein by weight and normal serving.

Are peas vegetables?

Culinarily yes; botanically they are legumes and contain more protein than most vegetables.

faq.question: Which vegetables contain the most protein?
faq.answer: Brussels sprouts, artichokes, kale, spinach and broccoli are among the higher common non-legume vegetables at roughly 3 g per 100 g.

faq.question: Is broccoli a high-protein food?
faq.answer: It contributes protein, but only about 2.8 g per 100 g, so it is not a concentrated primary source.

faq.question: Why exclude peas?
faq.answer: Peas are legumes botanically. If included as a culinary vegetable, they would rank higher at roughly 5–6 g per 100 g.
